replacementProcedure: Centrally inventory every consuming project and environment; this repository cannot establish the full shared-key inventory.
Receive the replacement through the hosting secret manager or an equivalent secure channel, never chat, logs, or the repository.
Update STRIPE_SECRET_KEY in each intended deployment environment; restart/redeploy all consumers because the Stripe client is cached per process.
Current validation accepts a standard secret key; introducing a restricted key requires a separately reviewed compatibility change.

API-key replacement alone does not require changing the endpoint signing secret or public key. If those are separately changed, update the relevant variables and rebuild native/web clients where public values are embedded.
Verify credential access, test checkout and signed webhook delivery/deduplication without real payments, using an isolated test environment.
Record successful migration of every project centrally before centrally revoking the old shared key.
If active exploitation is detected, escalate immediately to the central incident owner, preserve evidence, and coordinate containment/revocation across all projects.

remainingActions: Resolve the pre-existing CommonJS/ESM build configuration and invalid chat upload route export in a separate reviewed change, or apply the security patch to a known buildable production source snapshot. No deployment should promote an unverified build.
Restore authorized Vercel team/project access; inspect actual production build and function runtime versions plus deployment/source provenance before release.
Stage a security-only deployment from the known production source with these scoped changes, preserving unrelated workspace changes; verify before promotion.
Confirm all applicable managed runtimes and regions are patched using process.version/build logs/provider attestation, including cron/payment/webhook functions.
Verify future EAS build logs attest 24.22.1; independently inventory and update any external Node services or container images if discovered.
Review current Vercel runtime/firewall/audit logs and live Stripe API/security/webhook-delivery logs once authorized access is available.
Complete centrally coordinated shared-key cutover only when a replacement is supplied securely.
